sentences.ko: 걔 그렇게 급하게 나간 건 아니었나 보네.
sentences.text: Looks like she didn't leave in such a hurry after all.

alts.text: Guess she wasn't in that big a rush after all.
It appears that she did not leave in as much of a hurry as we assumed.

sentences.note: **after all**은 문장 끝에 붙어서 '생각했던 것과는 달리, 결국은'이라는 뜻이 됩니다. 내 예상이 빗나간 걸 알았을 때 씁니다. **in such a hurry**는 '그렇게까지 급하게'라는 말로, 서두른 정도를 두고 말할 때 자주 나옵니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 1 | Friends

sentences.ko: 달라는 값에서 한 푼도 못 깎아 준대.
sentences.text: They said they wouldn't go a penny under the asking price.

alts.text: Nope, they're not knocking a single dollar off what they're asking.
The sellers indicated that they will not accept anything below the asking price.

sentences.note: **the asking price**는 파는 쪽이 부르는 값입니다. 집이나 중고차를 살 때 그대로 씁니다. **a penny under**는 '한 푼이라도 아래로'라는 뜻이라, 값을 전혀 안 깎아 준다는 말을 강하게 할 때 붙입니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 10 | Friends

sentences.ko: 저녁 하라고 해 놓고 한 시간이나 늦게 와서는, 내가 부탁한 그거 하나를 까먹어?
sentences.text: You forced me to make dinner, then you're an hour late and you forget the one little thing that I asked you to do.

alts.text: So I cook, you show up an hour late, and you still forget the one thing I asked.
I prepared dinner at your request, you arrived an hour late, and you neglected the single task I had asked of you.

sentences.note: 늦은 정도는 **an hour late**처럼 시간을 앞에 붙여 말합니다('한 시간 늦었다'). **the one little thing that I asked you to do**는 '내가 부탁한 건 딱 그거 하나였는데'라는 뜻으로, 사소한 부탁을 잊은 상대에게 서운함을 드러낼 때 씁니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 10 | Friends

sentences.ko: 네가 카드 돌려줄 때 말이야, 네가 못 본 게 있는데 내가 눈에 안 보일 만큼 빠르게 봤거든.
sentences.text: When you handed me back the card, what you didn't see was I looked at it so fast it was invisible to the naked eye.

alts.text: So you gave the card back, and what you missed was me peeking at it too fast to catch.
As you returned the card to me, you did not notice that I glanced at it too quickly for the eye to register.

sentences.note: **handed me back**처럼 hand 는 '손으로 건네주다'라는 뜻이고 back 을 붙이면 '돌려주다'가 됩니다. **invisible to the naked eye**는 '맨눈으로는 안 보이는'이라는 굳은 표현으로, 너무 작거나 너무 빨라서 못 본다고 할 때 씁니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 3 | Friends

sentences.ko: 오웬이 입양한 게 우리한테 생긴 일 중에 제일 좋은 일이었어.
sentences.text: Adopting Owen was the best thing that ever happened to us.

alts.text: Best thing we ever did was adopt Owen.
Our decision to adopt Owen has been the most fortunate event in our lives.

sentences.note: **the best thing that ever happened to us**는 '우리한테 일어난 일 중 최고'라는 뜻으로, 사람이나 결정을 두고 크게 고마움을 표현할 때 통째로 씁니다. 주어 자리에 동사를 쓸 때는 Adopting 처럼 -ing 형으로 바꿉니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones That Make You Laugh: Part 3 | Friends

sentences.ko: 그럼 나도 남아 있겠다고 하는 게 낫겠네.
sentences.text: Well, then I might as well offer to stay.

alts.text: Guess I'll just say I'll stay, then.
In that case, I should probably offer to stay.

sentences.note: **might as well** 은 딱히 더 나은 수가 없을 때 "그럴 바엔 ~하는 게 낫겠다" 하고 마지못해 정하는 말입니다. **offer to stay** 처럼 offer to + 동사를 쓰면 "~하겠다고 먼저 말하다" 가 됩니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 3 | Friends

sentences.ko: 설마 공룡 옷 입고 갈 생각은 아니지?
sentences.text: Please tell me you're not going to dress up like a dinosaur.

alts.text: You're not seriously wearing a dinosaur costume, right?
I hope you are not planning to wear a dinosaur costume.

sentences.note: **Please tell me you're not** 은 "설마 그러는 건 아니지?" 하고 아니라는 대답을 바라며 확인할 때 씁니다. **dress up like** 는 무엇처럼 차려입는 것이라 할로윈·파티 이야기에 자주 나옵니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 8 | Friends

sentences.text: There is no such thing as bad press.

alts.text: Any press is good press.
Publicity is valuable even when it is unfavourable.

sentences.note: **no such thing as** 는 "그런 건 아예 없다" 고 딱 잘라 말할 때 쓰는 틀입니다. **bad press** 는 안 좋게 오르내리는 기사나 소문을 뜻하고, 구설수에 올라 곤란해하는 사람을 달랠 때 이 말을 합니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 8 | Friends

sentences.text: I'm just going to hang out as friends.

alts.text: We're just hanging out, nothing more.
I am only going to spend time with them as friends.

sentences.note: **hang out** 은 특별한 목적 없이 어울려 시간을 보내는 것입니다. 뒤에 **as friends** 를 붙이면 "연애가 아니라 친구로" 라고 선을 긋는 말이 됩니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones That Make You Laugh: Part 3 | Friends

sentences.text: Bathroom is down the hall to your left.

alts.text: It's just down the hall on the left.
The restroom is at the end of the hallway on your left.

sentences.note: **down the hall** 은 복도를 따라 쭉 간 쪽이라는 뜻입니다. 길을 알려 줄 때는 **to your left** 처럼 your 를 붙여 듣는 사람 기준으로 말합니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones That Make You Laugh: Part 3 | Friends
